name: Close-Location Absorption Run
note: A run of bars that keep closing near their high (CLV >= threshold each bar, mean above it) while the net close-to-close change is under a fraction of ATR, on wide bars and heavy volume -- the Volume-Spread-Analysis reading of a large seller being absorbed. Entry is the stop order through the run's extreme; the exit is a decisive close on the wrong end, the run's own low, or 10 bars.
source: Synthesis. The CLV statistic is the standard close-location term from the Williams Accumulation/Distribution and Chaikin Accumulation-Distribution Line constructions; the absorption reading (strong closes with no net price change on heavy volume) is the Volume Spread Analysis interpretation from Tom Williams, 'Master the Markets' (1993). The specific inequalities, the flat-price constraint and the CLV-based exit are my own quantification and have not, to my knowledge, been published or tested in this form.
